item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
Engineer避雷黑车某些毒Org，能够造成职场trauma的匪夷所思存在

和当事人及好些同事朋友家人讨论了，为了避免更多人受害，把这几年积累到的奇葩case分享如下：
1. 好manager留不住，坏manager飞黄腾达
黑车某些毒Org的组的manager是领导关系户，所以下面人深恶痛疾的manager可以活得好好的甚至快速青云直上。
有manager直接威胁IC，pulse survey是可以通过各种filter看出谁作答的，然后说那谁谁（该IC组里同事名字）竟敢给我打差评。此人甚至得意洋洋威胁下属，之前有人Pulse survey全给我打零分，除了自己换组（还是跳槽记不清了）又能怎样？
（只要有上司罩着）HR是没用的。极端case，被举报HR的有性骚扰case（有表白有未经允许肢体接触被拒绝后再次要求私下接触）被HR confirm的low performer manager换个Org能继续当manager，现在还在某个快速扩张的Org招人。

2. Credit归属可以完全颠倒黑白

曾经有同项目合作的时候，IC A去帮忙做了IC B搞不定的工作，结果B四处宣传全部工作是自己做的。A被同组人问起后纠正了，且说了B一直推说没bandwidth不干活。结果冠以gossip罪名被B告去HR。HR说调查后无违规，但A以后不可以评论工作的Credit是谁的。A问HR，你看这design doc，这meeting notes，这code，甚至analysis，visualization, 工作不都是我做的吗？HR说没人怀疑这个。A疑惑：所以为什么不能说这个是我做的？HR：Different people have different perspectives. 如果B的manager认为B做了，那么B就有Credit。
最后A因为合作问题被打了个low performer, credit似乎还真归了B（可能因为B和其manager拿着“借鉴”A的doc去跟高层present了）。
这个事情在Uber也不是偶发，之前甚至出现过过教授sabbatical来工作被抢Credit怒发邮件给高层的事件。当时邮件里面控诉之一就是， 当他escalate对方的剽窃行为，被对方污蔑不collaborative。

3. 某些Org Engineer地位极度低下，PM， scientist甚至OPs地位都能比Engineer高
比如上文2出现的终极原因可能只是A是个Engineer而B不是。Engineer manager甚至可以助纣为虐，帮着降低组里Engineer的visibility，比如纵容PM和scientist只拿Engineer干活不带Engineer出席任何有领导或者跨组的会。曾经有个case，全程implementation是Engineer做的，实验报告是Engineer写的，但是是PM和scientist去present的，大发慈悲带上了这个Engineer，但是要求会上此人全程不能开口（而此人竟然照做了）。

所以你要是个有想法有事业心的Engineer，加入黑车前最好打听下要加入的组，Engineer地位如何。否则去了这种干活背锅全是你，Credit和visibility都归别的function的，葬送大好青春不说，还可能惹上严重trauma，需要很长时间才能治愈那种。

➖ 传达室 ➖

item.title: 一亩三分地 - 热门帖子 热乎的485面试经验by sry 今天上午刚刚完成485面试经验 地点：Boston FO 面试官：一个有五个娃的白人大姐，看起来三十
item.description:
一亩三分地 - 热门帖子
热乎的485面试经验by sry

今天上午刚刚完成485面试经验

地点：Boston FO
面试官：一个有五个娃的白人大姐，看起来三十多岁

超过预约时间40分钟才被邀请进去面试（面试官说是系统有点问题导致的）。主申先进去的，面试房间就是一个普通的办公室，很小，基本跟面试官就是面对面。基本流程如下：
1. 宣誓，承诺回答真实有效
2. 查护照和ID、打双手食指指纹
3. 问基本信息（名字、生日、出生地、SSN、地址和以往地址、家庭信息、结婚日期、父母名字等等），无任何刁钻问题
4. 过485那一串yes no问题，按照填485时候回答就行
5. 过一份新的问卷，包括一些485上的yes no问题，也包括具体问是不是党员团员、是否接受过资助、什么时候出过美国国境、学都是哪里上的之类的。
6. 签字确认485有无改动。以及新的问卷也要签字，还另找了一个领导进来签字。
主申流程走完，副申进来走相似的流程，但是问题侧重有点不同：
1. 主申好久没出过美国国境了，所以面试官没咋问，但是副申六年前有一次回国记录，被具体问去哪见了谁干了嘛之类的。
2. 副申之前有一次B签证拒签经历，稍微问了一下，然后面试官在485上修改，然后让副申签字确认了。
3. 附加问卷部分，主申问的是团员，但是副申问的是少先队，不知道为啥。
最后问了一句，这卡嘛时候能下来，她说“should not be long“，"we already have all materials needed. We just need a security check and apply for a visa number”，“can do it as fast as I can”，其他就没啥了，总体很顺畅，没有什么刁钻的问题，也没有那种臆断性或者攻击性的预设立场。

10:40进去，11:35左右都面试完出来。主申API 11:35出现silent update，下午1:35出现FTA1，状态从interview scheduled变回currently processing。副申API在1:35出现silent update，但是没有FTA1。

据我的第一感觉，trigger这次面试的应该是那份额外的问卷，因为除了那个之外真的所有的东西都在485上了，只有那份东西是要很正式地签字确认的。个人猜测这有可能是总体面试率提升的症结。

最后希望那个所谓的“security check”就是个领导签字吧，最好卡快快批下来，真的等不起啊。。。_(:з」∠)_

➖ 传达室 ➖

超过预约时间40分钟才被邀请进去面试（面试官说是系统有点问题导致的）。主申先进去的，面试房间就是一个普通的办公室，很小，基本跟面试官就是面对面。基本流程如下：
1. 宣誓，承诺回答真实有效
2. 查护照和ID、打双手食指指纹
3. 问基本信息（名字、生日、出生地、SSN、地址和以往地址、家庭信息、结婚日期、父母名字等等），无任何刁钻问题
4. 过485那一串yes no问题，按照填485时候回答就行
5. 过一份新的问卷，包括一些485上的yes no问题，也包括具体问是不是党员团员、是否接受过资助、什么时候出过美国国境、学都是哪里上的之类的。
6. 签字确认485有无改动。以及新的问卷也要签字，还另找了一个领导进来签字。
主申流程走完，副申进来走相似的流程，但是问题侧重有点不同：
1. 主申好久没出过美国国境了，所以面试官没咋问，但是副申六年前有一次回国记录，被具体问去哪见了谁干了嘛之类的。
2. 副申之前有一次B签证拒签经历，稍微问了一下，然后面试官在485上修改，然后让副申签字确认了。
3. 附加问卷部分，主申问的是团员，但是副申问的是少先队，不知道为啥。
最后问了一句，这卡嘛时候能下来，她说“should not be long“，"we already have all materials needed. We just need a security check and apply for a visa number”，“can do it as fast as I can”，其他就没啥了，总体很顺畅，没有什么刁钻的问题，也没有那种臆断性或者攻击性的预设立场。

10:40进去，11:35左右都面试完出来。主申API 11:35出现silent update，下午1:35出现FTA1，状态从interview scheduled变回currently processing。副申API在1:35出现silent update，但是没有FTA1。

据我的第一感觉，trigger这次面试的应该是那份额外的问卷，因为除了那个之外真的所有的东西都在485上了，只有那份东西是要很正式地签字确认的。个人猜测这有可能是总体面试率提升的症结。

最后希望那个所谓的“security check”就是个领导签字吧，最好卡快快批下来，真的等不起啊。。。_(:з」∠)_

item.title: Avi Chawla How GPUs organize work, clearly explained: (popular AI engineering in
item.description:
Avi Chawla
How GPUs organize work, clearly explained:

(popular AI engineering interview topic)

A kernel launch can create millions of threads, but they don't all run at once.

The GPU assigns groups of threads to available sections of the chip. Within each section, it schedules instructions from threads that are ready to make progress.

The diagram follows this process, covering the function a program launches to the instructions the hardware executes.

1. The program launches a kernel

A kernel is a function containing the instructions the GPU should follow.

For this example, consider that each thread follows the same instructions, i.e., read two numbers, add them, and store the answer.

Each thread gets an index so it knows which pair of numbers to use.

2. Threads are organized into blocks

Rather than manage every thread separately, the program groups them into blocks.

Suppose there are 1,024 threads, grouped into blocks of 256. This gives four blocks.

Together, these blocks form the grid for this launch.

The GPU assigns blocks to its streaming multiprocessors, or SMs. An SM is a section of the chip that can execute threads.

All threads in a block run on the same SM. Multiple blocks can share an SM if enough resources are available.

3. The SM runs threads in groups of 32

These groups are called warps.

Our 256-thread block contains eight warps. When a warp executes the addition instruction, its active threads each add their own pair of numbers.

The grouping lets the hardware apply one instruction across many values.

If threads take different branches, some become inactive while others execute their branch. That means less work gets done by that instruction.

4. Waiting threads don't always stop other work

A thread needs its input numbers before it can add them.

If a warp is waiting for data, the SM can run an instruction from another warp that's ready.

Keeping several warps on the SM helps it find useful work during those wait times because if none are ready, the execution stalls.

5. Threads can also cooperate

Adding separate pairs needs no communication between threads, but there can be cases, like adding all those answers together, which require communication.

Threads within a block can exchange partial results through shared memory and synchronize before using them.

Combining results across blocks often happens in a later kernel, once the earlier work has finished.

The GPU therefore needs both enough work to run in parallel and a way to handle dependencies correctly.

Memory management is important as well.

Registers hold individual threads' working values, shared memory supports cooperation within a block, and L2 caches data across SMs. Larger HBM stores data such as model weights.

During LLM decode at small batch sizes, moving those weights can take longer than the calculations.

I covered that bottleneck in my RDU article, explaining how on-chip pipelines reduce data movement.

In my test, an RDU system using multiple chips generated 179 tokens per second, about 4x the estimated maximum for a single H100 running the same model at the same precision.

Read it below.

item.title: The Hustle What if a rideshare app only charged drivers $1 per trip? Most ride-h
item.description:
The Hustle
What if a rideshare app only charged drivers $1 per trip?

Most ride-hailing companies take a percentage of every fare.

This model charges a flat dollar.

That sounds tiny until you reach serious scale.

At 100,000 trips a day, that becomes $100,000 in daily revenue.

And the long-term ambition isn’t just rides.

It’s using that network to build financial products for drivers too.
